plan.summary: Deploy a two-service Cloud Run microservices mesh consisting of a Public API Gateway (gateway) and an Internal Core Processing Service (core-service) with OIDC service-to-service authentication, Secret Manager HMAC signing, Firestore persistence, and a daily Cloud Scheduler OIDC reconciliation job.
plan.architecture_overview: The workload deploys two Cloud Run v2 services scaling to zero when idle in a healthy region without Compute Engine VMs or VPC requirements. Service A ('gateway', primary service) exposes public HTTPS routes GET /health, POST /api/v1/orders, and POST /api/v1/reconcile. On POST /api/v1/orders, gateway validates payloads, mints a Google-signed OIDC identity token with the fixed audience constant 'https://service-b.orders.example', and calls core-service over HTTPS. On POST /api/v1/reconcile, gateway strictly verifies the incoming Bearer OIDC token against Google signatures, the fixed audience constant 'https://service-a.orders.example', and the workload service account email lazily fetched from the GCP metadata server on first request, before invoking core-service's internal reconciliation route. Service B ('core-service', internal IAM-protected service) exposes GET /health and internal routes (/internal/orders, /internal/reconcile), verifying on every /internal/ request a Google-signed OIDC token with fixed audience 'https://service-b.orders.example' and email matching its own metadata-server service account email, retrieving 'order-signing-secret' from Secret Manager to compute cryptographic transaction digests, and persisting order and reconciliation records in Firestore Native DB. Cloud Scheduler triggers POST /api/v1/reconcile daily at 02:00 UTC ('0 2 * * *') using the workload service account and audience 'https://service-a.orders.example'.

infra_tasks.title: Configure Workload Service Account and Least-Privilege IAM
infra_tasks.description: Create the shared workload service account used by both Cloud Run services and Cloud Scheduler. Grant roles/datastore.user for Firestore, roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor on the order-signing-secret, roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on itself so Cloud Scheduler and token flows can mint OIDC tokens, public roles/run.invoker (allUsers) on gateway, and authenticated roles/run.invoker for the workload service account on core-service.
acceptance_criteria: Shared workload service account is created

Gateway allows public HTTPS invocation while core-service restricts roles/run.invoker to the workload service account

infra_tasks.title: Provision Cloud Run Services (gateway & core-service) and Cloud Scheduler Job
infra_tasks.description: Provision Cloud Run v2 services 'gateway' and 'core-service' running as the shared workload service account with min_instance_count = 0 (scale to zero when idle). Wire CORE_SERVICE_URL and CORE_SERVICE_AUDIENCE to 'gateway', and ORDER_SIGNING_SECRET_ID and FIRESTORE_DATABASE to 'core-service'. Provision a google_cloud_scheduler_job running at '0 2 * * *' (Etc/UTC) sending POST requests to '${gateway.uri}/api/v1/reconcile' with oidc_token configured with service_account_email set to the workload service account email and audience set to 'https://service-a.orders.example'. Create path-filtered GitHub Actions deployment workflows for both services.
acceptance_criteria: Both Cloud Run v2 services scale to zero (min_instance_count = 0) and run under the shared workload service account
core-service requires IAM authentication and exports its URL to gateway via CORE_SERVICE_URL
Cloud Scheduler job runs at '0 2 * * *' UTC targeting POST /api/v1/reconcile with OIDC audience 'https://service-a.orders.example' and workload service account email
GitHub Actions workflows deploy gateway and core-service with path filtering

code_tasks.title: Implement Internal Core Processing Service (core-service)
code_tasks.description: Build the FastAPI application for Service B ('core-service'). Expose GET /health and internal routes POST /internal/orders and POST /internal/reconcile. Implement strict application-level OIDC token verification on every /internal/ route: require an Authorization Bearer token, verify its Google signature and exact fixed audience constant 'https://service-b.orders.example' (never reading Host header or request URL), lazily fetch and cache the runtime service account email from the GCP metadata server on the first request (not at module import time), and verify token['email'] equals that service account email—returning HTTP 401 or 403 otherwise. Retrieve secret 'order-signing-secret' (via ORDER_SIGNING_SECRET_ID) from Secret Manager, compute an HMAC-SHA256 cryptographic transaction digest over order data, write transaction records to Firestore (FIRESTORE_DATABASE), and support order reconciliation on POST /internal/reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Every /internal/ request verifies Google-signed OIDC token with exact fixed audience 'https://service-b.orders.example'
Service account email is fetched from GCP metadata server lazily on first request (never at import time) and verified against token email
Requests with missing/invalid token, wrong audience, or wrong email return HTTP 401 or 403
Order signing key is retrieved from Secret Manager to generate HMAC-SHA256 digests and store records in Firestore

code_tasks.title: Implement Public API Gateway Service (gateway)
code_tasks.description: Build the FastAPI application for Service A ('gateway'). Expose GET /health, POST /api/v1/orders, and POST /api/v1/reconcile. On POST /api/v1/orders, validate incoming order payloads with Pydantic, acquire a Google Cloud IAM OIDC identity token with the fixed audience constant 'https://service-b.orders.example' (not the target URL), and forward the validated order to '${CORE_SERVICE_URL}/internal/orders' with Authorization Bearer token. On POST /api/v1/reconcile, before doing anything else, verify the caller's Bearer OIDC token: check Google signature, exact fixed audience constant 'https://service-a.orders.example' (never using Host or request fields), and token email matching the workload service account email lazily fetched from the metadata server on the first request (not at import time), returning HTTP 401 or 403 on any failure; once verified, mint an OIDC token for 'https://service-b.orders.example' and invoke '${CORE_SERVICE_URL}/internal/reconcile'.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health and POST /api/v1/orders validate input and forward to core-service using OIDC audience constant 'https://service-b.orders.example'
POST /api/v1/reconcile verifies Google OIDC signature, exact fixed audience 'https://service-a.orders.example', and metadata-server service account email fetched on first request
POST /api/v1/reconcile returns HTTP 401 or 403 on missing token, invalid token, wrong audience, or wrong email before executing reconciliation logic

code_tasks.title: Implement Comprehensive Pytest Suite for OIDC, Metadata Server, and Order Flows
code_tasks.description: Write comprehensive unit and integration pytest suites for both 'gateway' and 'core-service' using mocked OIDC verification/minting, mocked GCP metadata server responses, mocked Secret Manager, and mocked Firestore. Explicitly test lazy metadata lookup (confirming importing modules makes zero network calls), valid order forwarding and HMAC digest persistence, core-service /internal/ rejection of missing tokens, wrong audiences (including Host-header spoofing attempts), and wrong service account emails, and gateway POST /api/v1/reconcile refusing a missing token, a wrong audience, and a wrong email with HTTP 401/403.
acceptance_criteria: Importing gateway and core-service modules triggers no metadata server or GCP client calls at import time
Tests verify gateway POST /api/v1/reconcile rejects missing token, wrong audience, and wrong email with 401 or 403
Tests verify core-service /internal/ routes reject missing token, wrong audience, and wrong email with 401 or 403, and persist HMAC-signed orders on valid auth
All pytest tests pass deterministically offline

plan.risk_assessment: Low operational and cost risk: serverless scale-to-zero Cloud Run v2 services, Firestore Native DB, Secret Manager, and Cloud Scheduler stay well under Tier 2 cost thresholds with zero Compute Engine VMs (inherently compliant with VM External IP prohibition) and defense-in-depth IAM + application-layer OIDC audience and identity verification.
